faq.a: Abdulhamid is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد, whose core sense is abdulhamid; servant of the praiseworthy.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulhamid?
faq.a: Abdulhamid is associated with Arabic. Abdulhamid is Arabic عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد (ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd), meaning 'servant of the Praiseworthy'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد is Arabic.
Abdulhamid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulhamid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdulhamid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdulhamid is rendered عبدالحمید and carries the sense عبدالحمید، حمید کا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdulhamid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdulhamid is rendered عبدالحمید and carries the sense عبدالحمید، بنده حمید.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-dul-ha-mid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdulhamid, abdulhamid. Script forms are عبدالحميد, عبدالحمید, عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد, अब्दुलहमीद.
